The best time to visit Bali for surfing is during the dry season, which is from April to October. During this time, the waves are consistent and the winds are favorable for surfing.

For beginners, some of the recommended beaches are Kuta Beach, Legian Beach, and Seminyak Beach. These beaches have small to medium-sized waves and are suitable for learning how to surf. There are also many surf schools and instructors available to help beginners get started.
<!-- SOURCE_TURN_001_END -->

对于初学者来说，推荐的海滩有库塔海滩、雷吉安海滩和水明漾海滩。这些海滩的浪花大小适中，适合学习冲浪。那里也有很多冲浪学校和教练可以帮助初学者入门。

1. Start with a surf lesson: Even if you're a strong swimmer, taking a surf lesson will help you learn important techniques and safety rules. 2. Be aware of riptides: Bali beaches have strong currents and riptides, so make sure to follow beach regulations and always surf with caution. 3. Rent beginner-friendly surfboards: Most surf schools or beach rentals offer soft-top surfboards, which are easier to handle and are safer for beginners. 4. Surf at the right time: Avoid crowded surf spots and research the best time to surf based on your skill level. 5. Protect your skin from sunburn and reef cuts: Wear a rash guard, surf boots, and apply sunscreen. 6. Respect the locals and environment: Bali has a strong surf culture, so respect local customs and keep the beaches clean. 7. There are many spas throughout Bali that offer affordable spa treatments. 3. Explore Bali's rice terraces: Bali's rice terraces are a must-see, especially if you're interested in photography. Take a cooking class: Bali is known for its delicious food, and taking a cooking class is a great way to learn how to make traditional Balinese dishes. 5. Go hiking or trekking: Bali has many hiking and trekking trails, such as Mount Batur, Mount Agung, and Campuhan Ridge. 6. Enjoy Bali's beaches: Apart from surfing, Bali's beaches offer plenty of other activities such as swimming, snorkeling, or just lounging on the beach.
